model.name: Owner-only access gate for Server Manager - server-side by-construction (owner 200 / non-owner 403, incl websocket)
model.description: The Server Manager UI AND every backing API/websocket are restricted to token 41ad88c4-4dee-49ac-afcb-8a2026657b2d, enforced SERVER-SIDE on every endpoint AND on the websocket handshake - the authenticated user's token is checked; anyone else gets 403 and never reaches the otmux/terminal APIs. UI-hiding alone is NOT acceptance. Correct-by-construction: a SINGLE owner-guard the endpoints share, not per-call ad-hoc checks. PAGE-ROUTE SCOPE (PO add 2026-07-20, architect forward-flag): R31.2's server-side owner-gate covers the /server-manager PAGE route itself (403/redirect for non-owner), not only /api/server-manager/* + the ws - the same shared assertOwner guard gates the page shell. Locked before R31.3/R31.4 build so the expert gates the page.
model.tronQuote: > TRON (2026-07-20): ONLY this user gets a new Server Manager ... owner-token-gated at the websocket handshake, not just the page; no path to the APIs for any other user

discoverySource.note: Sprint 31 Server Manager (owner-gated infra console), Tron-authorized. Minted scenario-first. UC method-set design-ahead PROPOSED; architect confirms the hard parts (esp. R31.4 PTY bridge + auth). #126 scenario-first.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Owner check is SERVER-SIDE on every Server Manager endpoint; the authenticated token is the source of truth (not a client flag).
Requests from token 41ad88c4-4dee-49ac-afcb-8a2026657b2d to every Server Manager endpoint + ws handshake succeed (200 / ws upgrade).
Requests from ANY other authenticated token to every Server Manager endpoint AND the ws handshake return 403 and never reach otmux/terminal APIs.
A SINGLE shared owner-guard (one function/middleware) gates all endpoints + the ws handshake - correct-by-construction, not per-call ad-hoc checks.

The websocket is gated at the UPGRADE, not merely the HTTP page: the shared owner-guard exposes an owner-gated HTTP endpoint that issues a single-use ~30s owner-bound TICKET; the ws upgrade validates ?ticket= and a non-owner (invalid/absent/expired/reused) gets 403 with the socket NEVER opening. Post-connect token checks are NOT acceptance (browsers cannot set ws auth headers). Per architect design 9920f6832.

The Server Manager PAGE route (e.g. /server-manager) is owner-gated SERVER-SIDE by the SAME shared assertOwner guard (single-literal): a non-owner request to the page route gets 403 (or a redirect away) and NEVER receives the page shell. Gating /api/server-manager/* + the ws ticket ALONE is NOT acceptance - the page itself is owner-only (Tron: 'ONLY this user will have access'). Client-side route-guarding / UI-hiding alone is NOT acceptance.

constructionInvariants.text: SINGLE guard, NO bypass: every Server Manager surface (page route /server-manager, /api/server-manager/*, and the ws ticket) passes through ONE choke-point (requireOwnerHttp/assertOwner). The page route has NO /api/ prefix, so the existing startsWith('/api/server-manager/') choke-point MUST be EXTENDED to also match '/server-manager' (gate both prefixes through the one guard) - NOT a second ad-hoc check. Stays on Impl 335dbf3d.
SINGLE OWNER_TOKEN literal: the owner token 41ad88c4-4dee-49ac-afcb-8a2026657b2d appears exactly ONCE (one shared constant the guard reads); no per-call/per-route re-literal of the token.

A REJECTED ws upgrade -> the socket NEVER opens and NO PTY is spawned (fail-closed at the handshake ticket check, not after connect). Symmetric with the ticket-at-upgrade gating in AC-ws-handshake / R31.4 AC-ws-owner-gated.

model.constructionInvariantsNote: Architect INV-G1/INV-G2 (2026-07-20), pinned scenario-first (correct-by-construction): the expert EXTENDS the existing choke-point to cover both '/server-manager' + '/api/server-manager/*' via the one assertOwner guard, single OWNER_TOKEN literal. Architect verifies the choke-point extension when the expert ships the page. These back AC-shared-guard + AC-page-route; the tester asserts non-owner-403 on ALL surfaces (page + api + ws) against the single guard.
